note:
The household of Robert Evans, architect, surveyor and justice of the peace, on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues.

**THE ADDRESS ON THE PAGE IS SOUTH ROAD AND THE HOUSE IS 11 CAVENDISH CRESCENT SOUTH (#43).** A. Hagues has settled it: this is a corner plot, and the enumerator wrote the road the door faces rather than the crescent the house is numbered on. The record's own listing description for #43 says so without meaning to - it notes the *later alteration and enlargement of main entrance porch adjacent to South Road*. The porch is on South Road; the number is on Cavendish Crescent South.

**Wright's Directory is not wrong either.** It prints *Robt. Evans, Esq, J.P., of Evans & Jolley* on South Road in 1894-95 and 1898-99, because that is the address the family gave. A corner house answers to both, and two sources agreeing on South Road is not evidence against the crescent - it is evidence that the family used the road their door opens onto.

**An earlier version of this file filed all twelve at 2 South Road (#381)**, on the stated ground that the record already held Robert Evans Sr there in 1911. That ground was false: his 1911 row is at **11 Cavendish Crescent South**, with another Evans, and Addis and Bellamy beside them. Twelve rows were created at #381 as a result and want deleting; this file now points at #43, so they will not come back.

**This is the same fault as Thorndale** - a corner house written under one street and numbered on another. It is worth suspecting wherever a household's address and its number disagree.

The family was already in the record without 1891, and each is bound by number: Robert Evans Sr (#405), and his children Edith Mary (#422), Alice (#423, 'Alice Ann'), Robert (#406, Robert Evans Jr, architect), Ethel (#424, 'Ethel Frances'), Mary (#425) and Dorothy (#426). The four servants and the visitor, Beatrice Elizabeth Clay, are new. The record also holds a second Robert Evans Jr, 'Robert Junior Evans' (#856, born 1863, at Ravine House in 1911), who is the same man and wants merging into #406.
source: 1891 census, South Road as the page has it - the house is 11 Cavendish Crescent South, a corner plot. Transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 136 (Leicester Special Collections id 164642); 1898-99, page 146 (id 165322).
